detailZh: F1 2027年赛历：摩纳哥将举办10场冲刺赛之一，以及下赛季赛程公布的其他看点
评估2027年F1赛季冲刺赛场次的增加（包括摩纳哥），以及这项运动赛程的其他变化；9月24日至26日通过天空体育 F1直播观看阿塞拜疆大奖赛的每一节练习，正赛在周六举行
克雷格·斯莱特解释为何摩纳哥被选为2027年F1赛季的冲刺赛举办地
F1的2027年赛历已经公布，下赛季再次安排创纪录的24个比赛周末。
但赛历中有若干引人关注的看点，包括冲刺赛场次的增加（以新增摩纳哥为头条）、这项运动惯常的中东分站继续保留，以及两条受欢迎赛道的回归……

正如7月所报道，F1将在2027年赛历中增加冲刺赛周末的数量。
冲刺赛的最终数量已确认为10场，比过去四个赛季每季的6场多出4场。
这一替代赛制于2021年首次引入，包含一场额外的排位赛来决定短程100公里比赛的发车顺位，它带来了全球电视观众的增长。F1表示，冲刺赛周末的观众比包含三节练习赛的非冲刺赛周末高出12%。
2027年的10个举办地平均分配于此前举办过冲刺赛的赛道——蒙特利尔、银石、蒙扎、英特拉格斯和卡塔尔的卢赛尔——以及首次采用该赛制的萨基尔、阿尔伯特公园、铃鹿、摩纳哥和阿布扎比的亚斯码头赛道。
目前的冲刺赛制（前八名获得积分）被认为在2027年将保持不变。
克雷格·斯莱特梳理2027年F1赛季赛历的主要看点，包括摩纳哥首次举办冲刺赛
为何摩纳哥将首次举办冲刺赛
当然，围绕2027年赛历的许多早期头条和争论都集中在摩纳哥意外地被列入10个冲刺赛举办地之一。
不仅这个公国此前从未举办过冲刺赛，其正赛为78圈，在狭窄、蜿蜒、围墙林立的赛道上本就不以超车著称，在干燥条件下比赛往往如同巡游。
通常正是排位赛——以及驾驶F1赛车在护栏之间全速穿行的挑战——成为摩纳哥周末最令人惊叹的部分。F1指出，增加冲刺赛意味着2027年将有两场这样的决定发车顺位的环节。
2026年摩纳哥大奖赛集锦
也可以说，只有一节练习赛而非通常的三节，为竞争格局带来更多不可预测性，因为车手只有一节练习赛来建立节奏和信心，而这是摩纳哥周末取得成功的关键要素。
“传统上，冲刺赛都在容易超车的赛道上举行。显然摩纳哥并非如此，”天空体育的克雷格·斯莱特说。
“但这里的一大好处是我们将有两场火热激烈的排位赛。这正是这条赛道的意义所在，车手们将在那个周末两次面临终极考验。”
明年将首次出现赛季以冲刺赛开始、也以冲刺赛结束的情况。
巴林将于3月12日至14日以该赛制揭幕赛季，而阿布扎比将于12月10日至12日收官。
赛季揭幕冲刺赛无疑将给车队和车手带来不同的挑战，因为他们那个周末只有一节练习赛来为赛季首个竞争环节——周五晚间的冲刺排位赛——做准备。
2026年英国大奖赛冲刺赛集锦
然而，在同一萨基尔赛道进行的季前测试（2月24日至27日）将为期四天而非三天——比通常非重大规则变更年份多一天——这意味着他们至少能熟悉这条赛道以及2027年的新赛车。
尽管如此，赛季揭幕冲刺赛仍代表着一项新挑战，如果车队未能充分掌握赛车和调校，可能会在赛季初的一个或两个发车顺位上带来意外。
赛季将以卡塔尔和阿布扎比的连续冲刺赛收官，这不可避免地带来一种可能：如果冠军争夺持续到最后一轮，世界冠军可能在周六的比赛中决出。
这已有先例，2023年卡塔尔站，马克斯·维斯塔潘在冲刺赛中锁定他的第三个世界冠军。
中东分站已排定，F1等待2026年的最终决定
这项运动的四场中东分站都出现在2027赛季，为24场比赛的赛季首尾相衔。
2026年计划中的最后两场卡塔尔和阿布扎比比赛同样如此，距离这项运动预定前往那里仅剩两个多月。
中东冲突已导致今年的沙特阿拉伯大奖赛取消，巴林大奖赛从原定4月在萨基尔赛道（吉达前一周）移至10月4日在马来西亚举行。
F1的意图和规划仍是2026年的最后两轮按计划进行。尽管斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利此前曾表示，关于这些赛事能否举行将在9月中旬有一个最终决定的时间框架，但据认为并没有硬性截止日期，官员们可以等待更长时间再做最终决定。
detailEn: F1 2027 calendar: Monaco staging one of 10 Sprints and other talking points from race schedule reveal for next season

Assessing the increase in Sprint races for the 2027 Formula 1 season, including Monaco, plus other changes to the sport's racing schedule; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
Craig Slater explains why Monaco has been chosen as a Sprint venue for the 2027 F1 season
Formula 1’s 2027 calendar is out with next season again scheduled to run to a record-equalling 24 race weekends.

But the schedule features a number of points of intrigue including an increase in Sprints, headlined by the addition of Monaco, the continued presence of the sport's usual Middle Eastern rounds, and the return of two popular tracks...

As reported in July, Formula 1 is increasing the number of Sprint weekends on the calendar for 2027.
The final number of Sprints has been confirmed as 10, four more than the six which have featured in each of the past four seasons.

The alternative format, which was first introduced in 2021 and features an additional qualifying session to set the grid for a short-form 100km race, has led to increase in global television audiences, which F1 says are 12 per cent higher than on non-Sprint weekends which feature three practice sessions.

The 10 venues for 2027 are split evenly between tracks that have staged Sprints previously - Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, Interlagos and Qatar's Lusail - and newcomers to the format in Sakhir, Albert Park, Suzuka, Monaco and Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina Circuit.
The current Sprint format, which features points for the top-eight finishers, is thought set to remain the same for 2027.
Craig Slater takes a look at the big talking points from the 2027 F1 season calendar, including a Sprint taking place in Monaco for the first time
Why Monaco is staging a first-ever Sprint
Certainly, many of the early headlines and debate around the 2027 calendar has centred on the fact Monaco has unexpectedly been included as one the 10 Sprint venues.

Not only has the Principality never hosted a Sprint before, its main 78-lap Grand Prix is already not known for overtaking around its narrow, twisty wall-lined circuit with the race often proving processional in dry conditions.

It is regularly Qualifying - and the flat-out challenge of threading an F1 car between the barriers - that proves the most jaw-dropping aspect of the Monaco weekend. F1 has pointed out that the addition of the Sprint means there will now be two such grid-setting sessions in 2027
Highlights from the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix

It can also be argued that having only one practice session, rather than the usual three, offers the chance for more unpredictability in the pecking order given drivers will only have one practice session to build rhythm and confidence, a crucial element of a successful Monaco weekend.
"Traditionally Sprints have been held at tracks where it is easy to overtake. Clearly that's not the case at Monaco," said Sky Sports' Craig Slater.
"But the big bonus here we'll have two red-hot qualifying sessions. That's what that track is all about and the drivers will have the ultimate test on two occasions that weekend."
For the first time next year, the season will both start and finish with a Sprint event.
Bahrain opens the season with the format on March 12-14 while Abu Dhabi will close it on December 10-12.

The season-opening Sprint will certainly present a different challenge for teams and drivers given they will have just one practice session that weekend to prepare for the campaign's first competitive session, Sprint Qualifying, on the Friday evening.
Highlights from the 2026 British Grand Prix Sprint race

However, pre-season testing at the same Sakhir circuit (February 24-27) will run to four rather than three days - one more day than is usually the case outside of years featuring big rule changes - meaning they will at least be familiar with the track with the new 2027 cars.
Still, the season-opening Sprint represents a new challenge and could offer some early-season surprises in the pecking order for one, or both, grids if teams are not on top of their cars and set-ups.

The fact that the season will finish with back-to-back Sprint events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi inevitably raises the possibility of the world title being decided in a Saturday race should the fight go down to the final rounds.
There is already precedent for this from Qatar 2023 when Max Verstappen clinched his third world title in the Sprint.
Middle East races scheduled as F1 waits on final 2026 decisions
The sport's four Middle Eastern races all feature on the 2027 season, bookending the 24-race campaign.
That also remains the case for 2026's final two scheduled races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi with just over two months to go until the sport is due to head there.

The conflict in the Middle East has already seen this year's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix cancelled and the Bahrain Grand Prix moved to Malaysia on October 4, having originally been scheduled for April at its own Sakhir track a week before Jeddah.

F1's intention and planning remains for 2026's concluding two rounds to go ahead as scheduled. Although Stefano Domenicali had previously indicated that there was a mid-September timeframe on making a final decision on whether the events could take place, there is thought to be no hard deadline as such with officials able to wait for longer before making a final call.
keyPointsZh: 2027年冲刺赛从过去四个赛季的6场增至10场，举办地包括蒙特利尔、银石、蒙扎、英特拉格斯、卢赛尔以及萨基尔、阿尔伯特公园、铃鹿、摩纳哥和亚斯码头。
2027赛季将以冲刺赛揭幕（巴林，3月12-14日）并以冲刺赛收官（阿布扎比，12月10-12日），这是历史上首次。
2027年赛历包含四场中东分站，而2026年卡塔尔和阿布扎比两站能否如期举行仍在等待最终决定。
keyPointsEn: The number of Sprints in 2027 rises to 10 from six in each of the past four seasons, with venues including Montreal, Silverstone, Monza, Interlagos, Lusail, plus Sakhir, Albert Park, Suzuka, Monaco and Yas Marina.
The 2027 season will both open with a Sprint (Bahrain, March 12-14) and close with one (Abu Dhabi, December 10-12), the first time this has happened.
The 2027 calendar includes four Middle Eastern rounds, while a final decision on whether the 2026 Qatar and Abu Dhabi races can take place as scheduled is still pending.

detailZh: 刘易斯·汉密尔顿：法拉利车队的七届F1世界冠军在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿周二访问了拉法口岸，实地了解向加沙运送援助物资的工作；这位法拉利车手周三在Instagram发帖，呼吁以色列“履行停火协议下的义务”。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿在访问拉法口岸后，呼吁以色列“放行援助卡车”进入加沙。
汉密尔顿周二在埃及，实地了解向加沙运送人道主义与救援物资的工作。这位法拉利车手还参观了拉法口岸，并走访了埃及红新月会的援助仓库。
美国支持的以色列与哈马斯之间的停火协议仍然有效，但并未结束以色列对加沙的打击，同时联合国世界粮食计划署表示，加沙三分之二的人口难以获得足够的食物。
汉密尔顿此前曾呼吁该地区实现和平，他表示援助物资因“疯狂的理由”被拒绝进入加沙。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的一条帖子。
您可以随时通过隐私选项更改您的设置。
这位七届世界冠军在Instagram上发文称：“过去三年以色列在加沙的种族灭绝行径令人震惊。”
“人们被剥夺自由、安全和尊严，这是不公正的。任何人都不应被当作生命不那么重要来对待。”
“我看到绵延数英里的围墙，是为了把他们困在里面而建的。站在外面，感觉就像一座露天监狱，我满脑子想的都是进去帮忙。”
“在拉法口岸，我看到食品卡车排着队准备出发，但它们经常不被允许进入，或者面临严重延误。我交谈过的排在第一位的那位司机已经等了超过12个小时。”
在附近的物流中心，我看到了救援人员的辛勤工作，但我也看到了因荒唐理由被拒绝的物资。睡袋、急救包、医疗设备、轮椅，甚至给孩子们的足球。
以色列需要履行停火协议下的义务，让援助卡车进入。没有任何借口。
我知道很多人都感受到同样的无助。同样觉得需要做点什么，而不是袖手旁观。我不想让我们对他们的苦难习以为常。我不想让我们移开视线。
周三，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡否认以色列在拖延物资进入加沙，并将加沙不断恶化的状况归咎于哈马斯，指责他们拒绝解除武装并截留援助物资用于军事用途。
2021年，汉密尔顿创立了Mission 44慈善机构，旨在支持年轻人并改善他们获得教育和就业机会的途径。
他还支持了人道主义和救援倡议，以及为受冲突影响的人们提供帮助的努力。
汉密尔顿是在上周末参加圣保罗大奖赛并获得第九名后进行了此次访问。他接下来将代表法拉利参加拉斯维加斯大奖赛，第一次练习赛于11月20日星期五举行。
汉密尔顿分享了与加沙儿童会面的细节
在首次发帖一天后，汉密尔顿于周四再次通过社交媒体分享了他与从加沙撤离的儿童互动的细节。
除了分享一组自己与孩子们的合影外，汉密尔顿写道：“在埃及见到一些由@inaraorg支持的从加沙撤离的巴勒斯坦儿童，我的心都碎了。
“这些美丽、聪明的孩子经历了创伤、悲痛和可怕的伤害，这些是任何孩子都不应该承受的事情。有些孩子在袭击中中弹或严重烧伤，仍在面对复杂的康复之路。但真正打动我的是他们如此坚韧，而且似乎在彼此身上找到了许多快乐。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿（@lewishamilton）分享的帖子

“当我问起他们的梦想时，他们谈到想成为老师和医生，这样就能像曾经帮助过他们的人那样去帮助别人。在经历了这一切之后，他们仍然想象着一个关爱他人的未来。这让我一直难以忘怀。
“我在学校、医院和一家心理健康诊所遇到了孩子们，帮助他们走出创伤。我还走进了一些家庭，倾听他们关于康复以及与亲人——他们的孩子、父母、兄弟姐妹——分离的故事。那种分离和不确定带来的痛苦令人难以理解。
“他们的故事让我想到了仍留在加沙的孩子们，他们生活在恶劣的条件下。据报道，自2023年10月以来，已有超过21500名儿童丧生，45000人受伤。他们每一个人都曾有过一个家和一个未来。我们不能忘记他们。
“这些孩子和你们的孩子没有不同。他们的生命同样珍贵。他们本应能在教室里与朋友相伴感到安全，与家人在一起，并憧憬未来。我非常感激我遇到的年轻人正在获得他们所需的帮助，但他们不得不离开家园去寻找安全，这令人心碎。”
加沙卫生当局表示，自2023年10月以色列开始对加沙发动攻势以来，已有超过74000人丧生。
以色列是在哈马斯武装人员对以色列南部发动袭击后发起这次攻势的，以方称该袭击造成约1200人死亡。

detailEn: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari's seven-time F1 world champion urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in' to Gaza after visit to Rafah border

Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border on Tuesday to witness efforts to transport aid into Gaza; Ferrari driver published Instagram post on Wednesday calling on Israel to "fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire"
Lewis Hamilton urged Israel to "let the aid trucks in" to Gaza after visiting the Rafah border.

Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.
Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.
"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.
"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.
"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.

"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.
"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.
"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.
In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.
He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.
Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.
Hamilton shares details of meeting children from Gaza
A day after his initial post, Hamilton took to social media again on Thursday to share details of his interactions with children he met who have been evacuated from Gaza.

Along with sharing a selection of photos of himself with the children, Hamilton wrote: "Meeting some of the Palestinian children evacuated from Gaza and supported by @inaraorg in Egypt broke my heart.

"Beautiful, bright children who have faced trauma, grief and horrendous injuries, things no child should ever have to endure. Some have been shot or badly burned in attacks and are still facing a complicated road towards recovery. But what really struck me was how resilient they were and how much joy they seem to find in each other.

"When I asked about their dreams, they spoke about becoming teachers and doctors so they could help others, the way they were helped. After everything they've been through, they still imagine a future caring for other people. That has stayed with me.

"I met children at school, in hospital and at a mental health clinic helping them work through their trauma. I also went into families' homes and listened to their stories of recovery and being separated from loved ones - their children, their parents, their siblings. The pain of that separation and uncertainty is hard to comprehend.

"Their stories made me think about the children still in Gaza, who are living in terrible conditions. According to reports, more than 21,500 children have been killed and 45,000 injured since October 2023. Every one of them had a home and a future. We can't forget them.

"These children are no different from yours. Their lives are just as precious. They should be able to feel safe in a classroom with friends, be with their families and imagine a future. I'm so grateful the young people I met are getting the help they need, but it's heartbreaking that they've had to leave their homes to find safety."
Gaza health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since Israel began its Gaza assault in October 2023.
Israel launched the offensive after Hamas gunmen led an attack on southern Israel, which it said killed around 1,200.
